record_type_quote: The technique was evaluated in a near replication of Bau and Mackay’s study protocol using a VR crib-sheet as a baseline.

targets.authors: Bau, O., and Mackay, W. E.
targets.title: Octopocus: A dynamic guide for learning gesture-based command sets
targets.evidence_quote: Our study replication also enables a direct comparison with Bau and Mackay’s OctoPocus in 2D.
targets.outcome_quote: Like our study, Bau and Mackay found OctoPocus significantly more accurate than a crib-sheet baseline, suggesting that OctoPocus is better at training people to perform more precise gesture movements in 2D and 3D. However, Bau and Mackay also found overall trial time for OctoPocus lower than crib-sheet, while we observed no overall difference in trial time, there is a trade-off between reaction time and input time. Bau and Mackay found no difference between conditions for input time or reaction time. In addition, Bau and Mackay found a significantly higher post-test recall for OctoPocus, but this appears to be because recall for our crib-sheet condition (83%) was much better than Bau and Mackay’s (57%).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparisons confirm accuracy and contrast overall time and recall. The general finding that VR OctoPocus is viable is not an overall replication verdict.

reasoning: Title, DOI and all five authors match. Full text includes the full article and references. Bau and Mackay reference 1 is the re-tested finding. Delamare et al. supplies guidance design recommendations and contextual benchmarks; its distinct feedback/feedforward experiments are not re-tested.
